name: Smartfish Product Filter
author: smartfish

sections.description:
Smartfish Product Filter adds responsive filters to WooCommerce product archives without changing your products.

The free plugin is complete, has no time limit, and does not require a license key.

Free features

  • WooCommerce categories and global attributes
  • Price, stock, sale, rating and keyword filters
  • AJAX result refresh
  • Vertical and horizontal layouts
  • Active chips, sorting and result-count shortcodes
  • Mobile filter drawer and RTL support
  • Unlimited filter sets, for WooCommerce products or any public post type
  • Checkbox, dropdown, radio, label and color-swatch displays
  • Automatic, apply-button and step-by-step filtering modes

Optional PRO upgrade

  • Custom fields, numeric ranges, dates and authors
  • Elementor widget
  • Import/export and one-click duplication
  • SEO index controls, automatic updates and Smartfish support

PRO is a separate paid package. The free plugin continues to work when no PRO license is present.

Shortcodes

  • [smartfish_filters]
  • [smartfish_filters set="123"]
  • [smartfish_filter_chips]
  • [smartfish_filter_sort]
  • [smartfish_filter_results_count]
sections.installation:
1. Install WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate Smartfish Product Filter.
  3. Open Smartfish Filters and review the default WooCommerce set.
  4. Add [smartfish_filters] to an archive sidebar or template.
sections.faq:
Is a license required for the free plugin?

No. Free filtering has no time limit and does not contact a license server.

Does the plugin change product data?

No. It reads existing WooCommerce categories, attributes, prices and stock data.

Does the free plugin contact external services?

No. It only contains optional links to Smartfish documentation and the PRO product page. An external request occurs only when an administrator chooses to open one of those links.

What data does the plugin store?

Filter-set settings are stored as a private WordPress custom post type and post meta. The plugin does not store visitor search or filter activity.

What happens if I later install PRO?

Existing Free filter settings remain in WordPress and are available to the PRO package.
